notes.title: Alpha v2 Released - Shipyard 7 Infestation
notes.content:
Alpha 2 Demo has been Released!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/92b3f8f0778b6ac568f89f5464f04157b5ecb19c.gif"]



This update brings all the features from last week's closed testing to the public demo - which includes a ton of new features, a teaser of the next stage's Interceptor production line area, 4 new enemies, and a quick look at a new massive mini-boss.

Grab and Throw small enemies,

New Enemies - Interceptor, Light Cruiser and Missile Cruiser, and some creepy crawly centipedes

Bullet Grazing and Bullet Sealing mechanics

New Scoring Mechanics

Entirely new areas and environments - Assembly plant with working conveyors and pneumatic stamping machines (smashers), and a centipede nest.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/27f13efd8b395ebf08dea9e2f0a66a4d1abd8c85.gif"]



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/0ddab2086040450d20f3536c58d26c81611f6653.gif"]



This is really just the beginning as far as what's to come in Cosmic Destroyer - new areas, a re-balance including more ships and weapons are just the around the corner - stay tuned as more features are coming very soon! Follow CoffeeMakerGames on Bluesky for live updates.



More details on the features included in the Alpha 2 release can be found in the dev roadmap update from last week:

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3712340/view/541113388287132111?l=english"][/dynamiclink]

notes.title: Game Mechanics Update and Dev Roadmap - (Alpha 1r2)
notes.content:
A cargo hold full of new features are coming!
This update is available to closed beta users and will be rolled out to the public demo next week on 8/14/25. The update is focused on adding a host of new game mechanics, and brings exciting updates to cover in detail. This includes updates to Grabbing, a new Missile type, Bullet Sealing and Grazing, as well as a complete overhaul of scoring mechanics and menu systems.

 
Where is Cosmic Destroyer Headed?
I am very excited to be charging towards 2DCON on August 22nd to 24th in Minnesota, where Cosmic Destroyer will be on demo at our booth on the Indie Island.

Here is a quick overview of the current development timeline for the next few weeks, which will bring more major updates every Thursday up to August 21st! There are even more exciting features planned, including an update to the Steam demo for Cosmic Destroyer on 8/14/2025 which will include a teaser of the new Shipyard 7 Stage – a nearby military installation constructing powerful ships for the defense of civilian colonies in the belt. It’s also the incursion point for the enemy force from the unknown.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/17aed22dac7129133c0c95d25e5ecc809d9ffd41.jpg"]

The plan going forward is to have a steady stream of updates with releases and roadmap updates every two weeks. Stay tuned for more updates, news, features. The ultimate goal is to release the full version of the game before the end of 2025!

 
Grabbing and Tossing Enemies
Small enemies such as Mining Drones, Scout Pods and Interceptors can now be grabbed just like special weapons by pressing the action button. 

A held enemy will provide special abilities based on the enemy type. These abilities range from firing at other enemies like a turret, altering your ship’s Primary or Secondary Weapons, or providing completely new abilities. You can also hold the action button after grabbing an enemy to charge up a throw maneuver which is being considered for other charge-up abilities as well! If that wasn’t enough, the enemy can be rammed into other enemies and used to protect your ship from projectiles while held.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/21eecc89d4c6f6e18a4f83e92e1a28be0bb4eaa7.gif"]

 
New Secondary Weapon: Lock On Missiles
This new secondary weapon locks-on to enemies within an area in front of the player’s ship while the fire button is held down. During that time, a lock-on reticle will be shown over targeted enemies. Upon release of the fire button, missiles are fired at each of the targets. These missiles trade stopping power for versatility, and are particularly well suited to hitting targets which are moving or positioned vertically in relation to the player. The maximum number of targets increases with missile power level and missile power-ups now cycle between the missile types which are available in the current game. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/2c06f83a3491a6818379658d1ade9c68ed95c7dc.gif"]



In Arcade Mode these power-ups will cycle as follows:

“M” Power-Up – Adds a missile of the current equipped type. If no missile was previously equipped, the default missile type for the ship will be used (generally Dumbfire Missiles).

“D” Power-Up – Switches to Dumbfire Missiles. If Dumbfire Missiles are already equipped the power level is increased, adding an additional missile. If another missile type is currently equipped, the missile power is reset to 1

“L” Power-Up – Switches to Lock-On Missiles. If Lock-On Missiles are already equipped the power level is increased, adding additional missile(s). If another missile type is currently equipped, the missile power is reset to 1



Note: some enemies being introduced soon will also fire Lock-On missiles which can be shot and destroyed. Missiles cannot be absorbed or grazed like normal bullets as they detonate when near a target and apply damage in an area.

 
Option Drone Power-Up Behavior
Option Drones currently provide a small score boost when they absorb an enemy projectile. Additionally, option drones which have absorbed a projectile become powered up for a limited duration, which increases based on the player’s Hit Multiplier. The projectiles fired from an empowered drone have a larger hit detection box and graphic, and do bonus damage. Option drones which collide with enemies and boss cores inflict damage, and this damage is also increased while powered-up.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/b919e723f585074d23cdc5015dfa8dc6181255e0.gif"]



 
Bullet Sealing
Getting up close and firing point-blank at an enemy is a risk which should be rewarded, not punished. While this was always planned, we’ve heard your feedback and have implemented this mechanic. Point-blanking bosses and spinning turrets is no longer certain death. Enemy firing logic will not create bullets if the player is right on top of them. This does not apply to charged lasers and other telegraphed special attacks such as jetstreams, flames, and missiles. The strategy of point-blanking works great with the damage buffs to option drone collisions and skilled players can use this dangerous strategy to maximize damage and take down enemies quickly.

 
Bullet Grazing
Bullet grazing mechanics allow a player to narrowly dodge a projectile to get an added bonus effect. This is generally reflecting the projectile back at a nearby enemy, which does heavy damage. Spread shots can be a powerful countermeasure to a screen filled with enemies – and this risk-reward pays off! In the future, we’d like to introduce more player choice to this mechanic, to allow players to chose the effect when grazing. These concepts range from trading reflected bullets for additional scoring, temporary power-ups, and temporary shields just to name a few.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/e98fbbeded88f8b5218068cb98ec761948d854fc.gif"]

A bit of a tease of the first area of the new stage "Shipyard 7" and some of the ships. This stage will be playable in the demo update coming next week on 8/14/25.


New Scoring Mechanics
In addition to the score pickups found in ground objects and when destroying complete enemy waves, additional score pickups can now be earned based on overall enemy destruction. Every enemy killed by a player is tracked, when enough enemies have been killed, a special score pickup is created which automatically is pulled into the player. The number of enemies required to spawn this score pickup is determined by the player’s current hit multiplier. The higher the multiplier, the fewer the number of enemies required to create a score pickup. Since the multiplier also applies to these pickups, this further incentivizes the player to make every effort to keep their hit multiplier high – because racking up a high score not only contributes to the leaderboard score but also results in additional lives at 50,000, 200,000 and 1,000,000 points.

 

There are a few more changes to mention related to scoring:

Each player’s Hit Multiplier no longer drains while transitions are occurring – as this was just not fair. It’s intended to be possible to complete all stages without ever losing your score multiplier.

Hit multipliers over 4X periodically create additional power-ups when enemies are defeated. Picking up a power-up which is already maxed-out provides a 100 point bonus (multiplied by hit multiplier, this is a substantial bonus).

Scoring bonuses are applied upon completion of the stage based on performance, which is outlined in “New Score Summary Screen”.

 
New Score Summary Screen
At the end of a stage, each player is now shown a progress report for the completed stage. This includes a roll-up of the following metrics, as well as bonus points awarded for performance in each area:

Ships Lost – A player which manages to complete a stage without losing a single ship is awarded a hefty reward of 10,000 points.

Bullets Canceled – Bullets cancelled either by grazing or special abilities such as power bombs are tracked here. 10 Points are awarded for each cancel

Enemies Defeated – Each enemy gives points when it is destroyed, but an additional bonus is given when reaching the end of the stage for all enemies. This bonus is 10 points per enemy. Additionally, if a high percentage of enemies are destroyed the player is awarded additional large bonuses:

100% Destruction – 100,000 points!

98% Destruction – 25,000 points

95% Destruction – 10,000 points

Enemies Defeated Visual Summary – All enemies encountered in the stage are shown as visual representation at the bottom of the scoring screen, each defeated enemy is shown as a darker version when defeated.

Objects like asteroids are grouped into one entry and may be removed from the “Enemies” classification in the future – as the only realistic way to destroy them all currently is by using bombs.

Finally, all totals for the stage are rolled-up and applied to the player’s total score for the current game session.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/6f1bb22c1b5adc554715779d185d3962bf6d7df6.gif"]

 

Reminder: Using a continue currently resets the player’s current score to zero when it is used. This is for the purpose of embracing the 1CC (One Credit Clear) goal of many skilled SHMUP players. In the future the plan is to replace this logic with flags for 1CC completions, which will have their own separate Leaderboard. We want to track each stage’s scoring and the over-all game session scoring non-destructively so players can see their score history in the future.


Menu Overhaul and UI Improvements
The entire menu system logic, as well as the visual style of menus has been overhauled to provide a better and more consistent experience. This also enables development of more dynamic menu layouts and flows in the future, and ability to configure and customize  menu style in the future.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/4887254afef1af27df991da1be52deaa4fdb2b1c.gif"]

 
Projectile Pattern and Enemy Spawn Determinism
Previously, when bullet patterns and enemies were spawned on the screen, their behavior could be inconsistent on different devices or depending on system performance. This was because the system was starting the logic for these entities based on the position of the object relative to the current scroll position of the stage, which could happen on frames which were not within a fixed, predictable timestep (which is used for behaviors, and physics calculations such as collisions). By ensuring that all projectile patterns and enemy initializations occur at a determined time, a much more consistent player experience can be ensured.

 
Bug Fixes
Collision Rework – the methods used for detection of collisions of ships and projectiles has been overhauled to support new grazing features and fix performance and false-positive collision bugs.

Fixed an error where the options menu remained active while closed.

Fixed an issue with game scroll position being inconsistent

Fixed an issue where stages would display slightly differently for users on Steam Deck or Linux compared to Windows. Arc Parameterization for splines has been overhauled to be more consistent when calculating rotation regardless of platform.

 
Platform Updates
Major performance improvements to Ship Manager and Projectile Managers, allowing for a 30-35% boost to maximum frame rate in busy scenes.

Future support for Alternate Game Modes has been added. The entire game’s high-level logic is now hot-pluggable, with systems such as ship loadout behaviors, upgrade paths, stage layout and composition logic all being configurable. This avoids any impact to code needed for other game modes which will be added in the future.

notes.title: Cooperative Multiplayer
notes.content:
I am pleased to announce that Local Cooperative Multiplayer has been added to Cosmic Destroyer! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/be2f423848f95fb11f5a4989a008a1d1bafb4303.png

Device Mapping
When choosing a game mode from the Main Menu, players can now select Co-Op and will be given the opportunity to choose which devices each player would like to control their ship. This functionality provides flexibility to support multiple devices for users that want to use non-standard setups like bearclaw. During development some very unique setups were tested including one with 2 gamepads, two keyboards and a mouse all working at the same time on one player - and another gamepad on the 2nd player.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/100257b70bfb14080f820b67d120bf3f6b194a8a.png

Each player can select their favorite ship and ready-up to jump into the game. Both players can select the same ship if they would like, there are no limitations.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/c92d5641b350e10cd522a3c22e9978dce1cfc411.png

Multiplayer Gameplay

Players have their own store of three lives and three continues, and all stats and scores are separate. When a player has consumed all of their lives they can continue by simply pressing the Action button, provided they have continues left to spend. If both players happen to game over at the same time, the standard Game Over screen will be shown to prompt the last player to continue. This screen is also shown if all lives and continues have been exhausted for both players.

Flair on the ships for each player is colored to match the Player Flag - Player 1 is Red and Player 2 is Blue. This color is also used in the UI HUD indicators in the upper left and upper right, respectively. The boss health indicator has been moved to be positioned at the top of the screen between both HUD elements and should be out of the way.

Device Disconnections
If a device which is currently mapped to a player is disconnected during play, the game will automatically pause. A notification message such as "Playstation Controller has been disconnected" will be displayed on the screen when this occurs. Generally whenever a player uses the pause functionality only that player can unpause or exit gameplay, but in cases of input device disconnection control may switch to the other player to prevent players from getting stuck having to force-quit due to input device issues.


Other notes and limitations
This mode currently does not allow for any High-Scores to be earned and is purely for having fun with your friends locally or using Steam's "Play with Friends" feature, provided a good network connection. Local leaderboards for co-op may be added in the future if there is interest.

Do note that split keyboard setups using one device across multiple players is not currently supported, mostly due to an engine limitation.

New Story Intro and Tutorial Dialogue
Captain Gerson now announces the mission's situation report to you with a virtual briefing before the game starts. The whole team is caught off guard by the initial attack, still the insight and information he provides offers context as to the situation around the Grid 38 Mining Facility and the attack on Shipyard 7. Sable, the ace pilot run the new pilot orientation tutorial, and you'll no doubt see more of her throughout the game. This also includes an ominous new backing track and new dialogue audio effects that really capture that retro feel. As development continues and we get closer to release there will be more information to share and new characters to meet. Although I want to be careful not to spoil anything by revealing too much before the final game release, either!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/f2ac15b34ca565011b3c0b2fdd4eb405e5d743f8.png

notes.title: Game Options, Settings and Training Mode
notes.content:
Since the initial announcement of Cosmic Destroyer going on Steam earlier this week, my focus has been getting a public demo ready for release for players to try it out. In order for that to really work, players need to be able to configure the game so that it can run properly on their systems. That means that players at the very least need options for display and controls.  Building these option menus and functionality, while vastly improving performance have been the focus of all development effort this week.

Option menus have been added to Cosmic Destroyer to allow players to customize their experience, remap controls and adjust audio and video options. This also includes the addition of a Training Mode for learning the game and the stage layouts, like enemy, power up and destructible object's spawn locations. This is the first of many game modes, expect many more in the coming months as Cosmic Destroyer blasts off towards launch.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/0ece3a20a11de6a33a2011d2c412812b13701382.png
Training Mode
This mode provides the player with unlimited continues and bombs, and starts the player out with maximum power level, secondary weapons (missiles, etc.) and option drones. When starting a game in Training Mode, the player will be allowed to choose from any starting stage in the final game. Training Mode play-throughs cannot earn achievements or register a high score. A "Training Mode" message callout and watermark are added to the screen.

Options
The following option panels have been added accessible from the main menu.

Game
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/f2c1df753700ed9a8cab3b7034c67ecf0f7e3702.png
General game options not related to the current game session/mode are found here

 Show hit box - shows a brightly colored box exactly matching the size and position of the hit box on the player at all times. This is rendered on top of all other content, even the UI.
 Show Hints - the game often prompts players "Shoot" or "Pick up" the first time they encounter certain objects like cores to shoot to open doors or destroy bosses. This is helpful for new players but can be turned off here.
 Show Tutorials - the first stage involves a section that will wait for player input and introduce a wave of enemies slowly before continuing. This slow progressing section can be disabled here
 Arcade Marquee - A video of gameplay is shown after short time to prevent screen-burn-in and showcase the gameplay. In the future this footage will be replaced with mix of recent high score replays from the player and the top replays from leaderboards. 


Video
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/a87b38a6aadd5f2a60e026d4440acbdb1c09381d.png
No game is complete without proper video options. The game is intended to be always run at 16:9 resolution, and letterbox / pillarbox is displayed to fill the screen while maintaining a consistent game experience and fair play area to all players regardless of display configuration.

 Display Mode - options include Windowed Fullscreen, Fullscreen and Windowed
 Resolution - your monitor's resolutions and refresh rate variations can be selected here
 V-Sync - Vertical sync smooths screen tearing when game and monitor refresh speeds do not match
 Brightness - Simple gamma brightness adjustment.
 Quality - (This section is coming soon as it needs a few visual improvements for quality presets) includes options to reduce particle quality such as distortion effects, or reduce particle counts for systems with low-end GPUs which struggle with overlapping transparencies.


Audio
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/d4d6013bfb0e9cc0e97f441f8f0092a1fbc93ca9.png
We hope you always want to play Cosmic Destroyer at full blast in a loud arcade - but also recognize you might want to play your own music or duck the audio for streaming.

 Main - Main volume of all sound
 SFX - sound effects such as weapons and explosions
 Voice - announcements such as "Power Up" and "Game Over"
 Music - music, set to however much synthwave you can handle!


Control
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/3cd931b3e3aab906d04891e048e18d40c804f765.png
Here  you can remap your controls inside the game. Provided are Primary and Secondary mappings with the defaults set to Keyboard and Gamepad bindings. Steam's Mapping should handle scenarios for mapping through that method as well, but provided here to aid with setups such as Keyboard mapped arcade controllers and other customizations.


One last nerdy development note on performance - it's always been a deal-breaker any time the game drops below 60FPS for any reason. It's a "drop everything and fix whatever is causing the slowdown" moment. It is particularly important in these types of games which simulate at their own internal tick of 60FPS. This must be done to ensure reliable movement, collisions, and in the end - scoring. This week, I've also gone through and deeply researched every memory allocation and process time and radically optimized for the smoothest experience possible, to get the game running well even on slower machines. Glad to say that currently, the frame update uses exactly 0 bytes of heap allocation - so NO garbage collection necessary, which avoids random frame drops. On a decent gaming PC I've pushed into well over 200FPS - even when forcing the logic to fully update every single frame. That's good news for anyone who appreciates a smooth gaming experience!
